note: Both sets cover the dinner-party safety rules and the Home Electronics display requirements, and each contains one substantively misbound claim plus several near-duplicate restatements. Set A invents a condition and a fabricated quote for the flames rule ("during cooking/preparing the meal" instead of "during contest week") and narrows the alcohol prohibition by rewriting "served, or part of a meal" as "served as part of the meal"; otherwise its values, units and conditions track the page (27 in/68.6 cm TV, 15 in/38.1 cm computer, 75% brightness, sealed-container water, cooler rules, host-team functions, wastewater). Set B misstates the food/beverage storage requirement as "manufacturer's instructions" with an invented quote (the text says instructions on the packaging) and paraphrases several quotes so they no longer match the source (non-decathletes "in the preparation of the meal" vs "in any way"; food prep "during the competition" vs the Appendix A-3 period; "as shown in" vs "designated in" the drawings), plus a garbled "d'oeuvres" entity. Set B does add facts A omits (meal served in finished square footage, hors d'oeuvres may be served outside, non-decathlete restriction, in-house food preparation), but A omits fewer distinct rules overall and is more quote-faithful.
